content: Aluminium chloride is a chemical compound that has been approved by the FDA for use in controlling minor bleeding during dental restorative procedures. It is commonly used in professional dental settings and is not intended for general or unsupervised use. To control minor hemorrhage during dental procedures, a small amount of Hemoban (a product containing aluminium chloride) should be dispensed into a clean dappen dish or disposable cup. For cases where hemorrhage control is needed before taking a restorative impression, a retraction cord should be soaked in aluminium chloride. This cord is then placed into the gingival sulcus using a cord-packing instrument. Aluminium chloride is compatible with all impression techniques, but it is recommended to gently rinse critical areas with water before applying addition-type (VPS) impression materials to avoid interference with the setting reaction of the impression material. For other minor hemorrhage control situations, a cotton pellet soaked in aluminium chloride can be applied to the affected area for several seconds, followed by a gentle rinse with water. Aluminium chloride should not be used in individuals with known sensitivities to the compound. It is strictly for professional dental use and should not be swallowed. It must be kept out of reach of children. The most common adverse reaction associated with aluminium chloride is hypersensitivity. There is limited information available regarding its use in pediatric, geriatric, pregnant, or nursing populations, as well as in individuals with renal or hepatic impairment, specific gender or racial groups, or immunocompromised patients. No specific guidance exists for its use during labor and delivery. Aluminium chloride is applied topically, and its mechanism of action involves controlling minor bleeding during dental procedures. It is often used with a cotton pellet or retraction cord and typically contains 25% aluminium chloride. There is no detailed information available regarding its pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, or nonclinical toxicology. The product should be stored at temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) and protected from freezing. There is no established interaction between aluminium chloride and alcohol, but patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol consumption while using this medication. The brand name for aluminium chloride is HEMOBAN®.
